change.title: pr-7
change.description: scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes
change.author: Jeff Atwood

findings.title: Reply-meta username color is inverted for both themes
findings.body: `dark-light-choose` returns its first argument on light themes (common/foundation/variables.scss:46-51), so light themes should keep the old `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. This line uses `$primary` 70% for light and `$secondary` 30% for dark, which swaps the two values. On light themes the bold username in `.topic-meta-data h5 a` is now much paler (70% instead of 30%). On dark themes it gets the dim value instead of the bright one. Every other line in this PR follows the `(N%, 100−N%)` pattern, so this should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message-length color is inverted
findings.body: The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, and the desktop version of the same rule (desktop/modal.scss:94) correctly became `dark-light-choose(…$primary 70%, …$secondary 30%)`. Here the arguments are swapped to `$primary 30%` and `$secondary 70%`. On light themes the hint text becomes much darker than before. On dark themes it becomes brighter than desktop. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The PR is meant to add a dark-theme branch, but this line also changes the light-theme value: it was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `$primary 50%`. The desktop counterpart (desktop/topic-post.scss:321) keeps 20%/80%. On light themes the mobile `h3` text is visibly paler than before. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

findings.title: Group member name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, and the replacement uses 50%/50%. That changes the light-theme color of `.group-member-info .name`, which now matches `.title` (line 527) and loses the difference between the two. To keep the existing light look and add the dark branch, use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The same change is in mobile/user.scss:497.

findings.title: Mobile group member name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: This is the same mistake as desktop/user.scss:522. The old `$primary 30%` became 50%/50%, which changes the light-theme color and makes `.name` the same as `.title` (line 503). It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

summary: The PR claims it only adds a dark-theme branch: each `scale-color($primary, N%)` is wrapped in `dark-light-choose(…$primary N%, …$secondary (100−N)%)`, and light themes keep their current colors. `dark-light-choose` returns its first argument on light themes (common/foundation/variables.scss:46-51), and most of the edits follow that pattern correctly. Five lines break it and change colors on light themes too. Two have their arguments swapped: desktop/topic-post.scss:291 and mobile/modal.scss:102. Three change the lightness value: mobile/topic-post.scss:182 (20%→50%), desktop/user.scss:522 and mobile/user.scss:497 (30%→50%).
